title: Your next campaign topic is in your support queue
metaTitle: Event and campaign topics for IT firms
description: People come to an event, read an e-book or join a workshop to fix a problem they have. Pull your tickets and name the campaign after the commonest one.
dek: Pick a campaign topic on a hunch and the workshop can fill up with your own staff. The topics people turn up for are in your support queue.
author: Shane Kennedy

video.title: The support queue. Marketing for IT firms

images.alt: “Your next topic is in support” in bold capitals, beside a man covered in sticky notes

shortVersion: Your support tickets list the problems your next campaign should be about.
People come to an event or read an e-book to fix a problem they have.
Pull three months of tickets, find what comes up most, name the campaign after that problem, and get it to people who aren't clients yet.

beats.heading: Events, e-books and workshops
body: When a lot of organisations are deciding which campaigns to run, they often just go with what they think is going to hit. That can be the service they'd most like to sell.
But the reason people come to an event, read an e-book or attend a workshop is to fix a problem they have.

graphic.to: To fix a problem they have
graphic.caption: Illustration

beats.heading: When the topic misses
body: If your campaigns don't line up with this, no one's going to turn up to your event, nobody's going to read your e-book, and your workshop's going to be filled with internals, just trying to boost the numbers.
A room full of your own staff might look fine in the photos, but nobody in it is going to become a client.

graphic.eyebrow: What happens when the topic misses

steps.text: Topic picked on a hunch about what will hit
It doesn't match a problem people have

beats.heading: Start with three months of tickets
body: Step one: pull the last three months of tickets, or the questions clients ask.
Step two: find the recurring themes, the questions that come up the most.
You don't need a reporting tool for this. Export the ticket subjects into a spreadsheet and sort them into rough groups. Ask the service desk too. They might know the top few without looking.

beats.heading: Name it after the problem
body: Step three: name your campaign after that problem. Something like "Why your Microsoft 365 bill keeps going up".
Anyone paying that bill knows the title's about them before they open the invite.
Step four: get it out to people who aren't clients yet. They're the firms still living with the problem.
